ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, including foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any material change in ownership or control. All results must be documented and retained for at least 5 years. For this medium-risk wholesale copper trading entity, additional scrutiny is applied to transactions involving high-risk jurisdictions, cash payments, or complex ownership structures. The compliance officer must approve any transaction exceeding USD 10,000 with a PEP or sanctioned entity. Failure to screen or report suspicious activity may result in criminal penalties under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Registry Office (법원등기소) – Online Name Clearance via IREG (Internet Registration System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean script (Hangul). Foreign names must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul. The name must include the liability suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' (주식회사). The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) trade name (상호), (2) object clause (목적), (3) capital amount (자본금), and (4) liability type (책임형태). The trade name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Chapters II and III, particularly Articles 289 (modes of incorporation), 290 (contents of articles of incorporation), 295 (payment of subscribed shares), 302 (registration of incorporation), 317 (time of corporation registration), 330 (total number of shares authorized), 383 (board of directors), 389 (representative director) and 415 (auditor); Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 2, 4, 5 and 27, and Enforcement Decree Articles 2, 5 and 9.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division, Civil Affairs Office, Local District Court (Beopwon Deung-gi-gwa) having jurisdiction over the principal office of the company, National Court Administration, Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Incorporation Registration (Hoesa Seollip Deung-gi Sinscheongseo) together with the duly notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act of Korea does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, all subscribed shares must be fully paid at incorporation, and the subscription funds must be deposited into a blocked incorporation subscription account with a licensed Korean bank or securities company and must remain restricted from withdrawal until registration of incorporation is completed. This blocked deposit rule is derived from Article 295 of the Commercial Act. If a foreign investor subscribes and the investment amount is KRW 100,000,000 or more and the investor holds 10% or more of the shares, the transaction must be processed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to qualify as foreign investment, with notification made to KOTRA Invest Korea or an authorized foreign exchange bank. The official registry cost is not a flat USD amount: registry fees are an ad valorem 0.4% registration tax on declared capital, plus 20% local education surtax, plus the court registry filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA. HELD ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], REPUBLIC OF KOREA. PRESENT: [DIRECTOR 1], [DIRECTOR 2], [DIRECTOR 3]. IN ATTENDANCE: [AUDITOR OR NOTARY]. WHEREAS the Company has been organized for the wholesale physical arbitrage of Grade A refined copper cathodes and incidental trading, storage scheduling and delivery activities under ISIC 4662; and WHEREAS the incorporators have subscribed for and paid in the issued ordinary shares of the Company. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The authorized share capital of the Company is [KRW ] divided into [ ] ordinary shares of no-par value, and the total number of issued and paid-in shares is [ ] ordinary shares. The subscription ledgers, share allocation records, the Certificate of Paid-In Capital Deposit issued by [BANK] from a blocked incorporation subscription account, and the shareholder register schedule are ratified in full. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Representative Director is authorized, individually, to open, operate and close domestic and foreign currency bank accounts with [BANK], to appoint authorized signatories, to complete KYC and AML onboarding documentation, to execute documentary letter-of-credit applications, and to give instructions relating to LME warrant transfers and settlement proceeds. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Company is adopted as [ADDRESS, REPUBLIC OF KOREA]. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the lease, obtain the corporate seal, order the office nameplate and complete all address registration requirements with the court, tax office and local government. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [NAME] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] is appointed Inside Director, and [NAME] is appointed Auditor. Each officer shall hold office for the term stated in the Articles of Incorporation and shall serve without automatic compensation unless otherwise fixed by resolution. 5. GOVERNANCE AUTHORIZATIONS: The Representative Director and the Company Secretary are authorized to submit the Application for Corporation Incorporation Registration to the competent District Court, to pay registration taxes, to obtain certificates of incorporation and corporate seal, to file the Business Registration Certificate application with the National Tax Service, to register the workplace with social insurance authorities, to complete Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration if applicable, and to execute all ancillary legal instruments. 6. RATIFICATION: All pre-incorporation contracts, deposits, account openings, and preliminary governmental notifications made on behalf of the Company are ratified, confirmed and adopted. 7. EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force until amended or revoked. A certified copy shall be attached to all bank mandate and court filing documents. ACCOMPLISHED AND ORDERED by unanimous vote of the directors at the above meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation, Share Subscription and Blocked Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office of the National Court Administration (IRO/Cereg portal) and an authorized foreign exchange bank or KOTRA Invest Korea window for foreign investment notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporation counsel shall first verify availability of the proposed corporate name, prepare draft Articles of Incorporation, and obtain each subscriber's written acceptance. The directors-designate will open a temporary blocked incorporation subscription account at a licensed Korean bank, execute share subscription statements, and remit the full subscription price into that account. The bank will issue a Certificate of Paid-In Capital Deposit expressly reciting that funds cannot be withdrawn until registration of incorporation is completed. If a foreign investor subscribes and the investment equals or exceeds KRW 100,000,000 with 10% voting shares, a Foreign Investment Report must be filed before or contemporaneously with the deposit in order to preserve the rights and protections of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
required_dossiers: Passport or corporate certificate of each incorporator or subscriber
Certificate of Paid-In Capital Deposit issued by a licensed Korean bank
Foreign Investment Notification receipt, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected due to identity or similarity with an existing trade name, select two alternative names and resubmit through the same IRO portal. If the deposit certificate is deficient, have the bank correct the account caption or complete a new blocked deposit and issue a clean certificate within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize Articles, Hold Initial Meetings and File Incorporation Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil Affairs Registration Division of the local District Court; also available through the CEREG electronic registry filing service of the National Court Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of capital deposit, the incorporators shall have the Articles of Incorporation notarized by a Korean notary public, execute the formal incorporation subscription statement, convene the initial general meeting, elect directors and auditor, and adopt the First Board Resolution. The registration representative shall file the Application for Corporation Incorporation Registration, pay the ad valorem registration tax and court filing fee, and complete seal registration. The court registry will examine the articles, subscription minutes, deposit certificate, foreign investment notification, and director identity documents. Once accepted, the court issues the Certificate of Corporation Registration and a certified corporate registry extract. This step must be completed within two weeks from the payment date or from the approval required under Article 317 of the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the incorporators meeting and first board meeting
Signed and sealed consent of each director and auditor
Foreign Investment Report certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplemental order (bocheong), the deficiencies must be cured within the stated period, normally ten calendar days. If the application is rejected for defective notarization, re-notarize and re-file without paying registration tax again where the original tax voucher remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Phong State? Register for Business Tax, VAT and Customs Identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Section of the local District Tax Office (Semo) under the National Tax Service, and Korea Customs Service for importer-exporter registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty calendar days after court-issued incorporation registration, the representative director must file an application for Business Registration Certificate at the tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office. The application must state the exact trade name, place of business, ISIC 4662 wholesale metals classification, and corporate tax domicile. The tax office will issue the business registration number, the electronic tax invoice certificate, and assign corporate tax and VAT compliance obligations. If the company will physically import or export copper cathodes, the company must register as an importer-exporter at Korea Customs Service. This customs registration is a mandatory trading right registration, not a discretionary operational license. The Business Registration Certificate must be displayed at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease agreement or ownership deed
Passport or national ID of representative director
Board resolution authorizing tax agent, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the active nature of the office, provide evidence of actual use including lease, signage, utility bill, and photographic proof. If rejected due to incomplete address documentation, amend the registered office and resubmit on the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Social Insurance, Labor and Occupational Safety Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service, and Ministry of Employment and Labor, using the unified Four Social Insurances one-stop online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fourteen days after hiring the first employee, the company must file the workplace establishment notification through the integrated social insurance online system or at the local National Pension Service. The company must obtain employer registration numbers for national pension, national health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance. If the company operates inventory inspection or warehousing areas for copper cathode physical transfer, an initial occupational safety and health risk assessment must be documented and posted. For a director-only company, the representative director may be enrolled for national pension and health insurance only if remuneration is paid; otherwise a non-coverage confirmation may be requested.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation and First Board Resolution
List of employees with resident registration or passport data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an administrative query is raised, respond with employment contracts and wage evidence within ten calendar days. Eligibility for voluntary declaration under the social insurance collection rules can avoid aggravated late charges if corrected promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration and Open Operating Banking Trade Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Invest Korea and the authorized foreign exchange bank; Korea Customs Service for importer-exporter code activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the initial foreign investment report was made, the foreign investor must complete the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration after incorporation through KOTRA Invest Korea or the authorized foreign exchange bank. The company must also activate the Korea Customs Service importer-exporter code to permit customs declarations for documentary LCs and physical copper cathode movements. The certified First Board Resolution is then delivered to the bank to open operating accounts, complete beneficial owner KYC, activate internet banking, and arrange documentary credit and LME warrant settlement protocols. The bank AML compliance officer may require the copper cathode supply chain documents to verify the commercial substance of the funds flowing through the accounts.
required_dossiers: Passport of representative director and beneficial ownership declaration
Certified First Board Resolution and bank mandate forms
Master copper cathode trade agreement or contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or customs office suspends the application for KYC clarification, respond with corporatedocumentation on the trade chain including documentary LC, bill of lading, warehouse receipts and LME warrant records. Corrected beneficial ownership declarations will allow the competent authority to resume processing within five business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for pure wholesale and physical arbitrage of Grade A copper cathodes. There is no manufacturing, smelting, refining, chemical processing, assembly or industrial treatment operation. If the company later establishes a warehouse, container yard or depot exceeding local building thresholds, the competent authority becomes the Municipal District Building Division (Si/Gun/Gu) and the local fire safety inspection office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. The only administrative prerequisites are the Business Registration Certificate (Saeopja Deungrok) under the Value Added Tax Act and, if regularly importing or exporting copper cathodes, the Importer-Exporter registration code issued by Korea Customs Service. Copper cathodes are not strategic goods requiring a separate export or import license under the Foreign Trade Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and its regional environmental offices; only relevant if a terminal, container yard, or warehouse with supporting heavy equipment is constructed later.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. Office-based wholesale trading under ISIC 4662 is exempt from the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. Should the company subsequently build or operate a storage facility handling only whole copper cathodes, the tier is generally a Small-Scale Environmental Impact Review under Article 22 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. If the facility also includes waste treatment, electroplating, or effluent discharge, a full EIA Report would be triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable to pure wholesaling. If a future warehouse includes wash-down areas, the company must comply with the Water Environment Conservation Act effluent standards, including 5-day BOD of 40 mg/L, suspended solids of 40 mg/L, and no cyanide discharge. Noise from fans or vehicles must meet the Noise and Vibration Control Act daytime workplace limits. Copper cathode handling does not create VOC or particulate emission quotas.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to the registered office. If a manned warehouse is established, the operator must obtain a Fire Safety Completion Certificate under the Fire-Fighting Facilities Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Management Act, a Fire Protection System approval from the National Fire Agency, and an Occupational Safety and Health start-up declaration to the Ministry of Employment and Labor before operations begin.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea, via the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr). Customs export clearance and export declaration administration is under Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Chusik Hoesa or a foreign non-resident entity with a Korean domestic place of business: (1) obtain the legal corporate registration and proof of a fixed establishment in Korea; (2) submit a Business Registration Application to the competent district tax office of the National Tax Service, online through HomeTax or in writing at the local tax office, within 20 days after the date of business commencement; (3) attach the articles of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, passport or director identification for foreign directors, evidence of registered business address in Korea, and, for a foreign entity, evidence of its domestic place of business and the appointment of a Korean tax representative if required; (4) receive the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the single statutory TIN and VAT registration number used for all NTS filings, e-tax invoices, VAT returns, corporate tax returns, and customs export documentation; (5) for a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean fixed establishment that still has Korean VAT filing obligations, register for simplified VAT registration through HomeTax through a Korean tax representative. Any later change of business location, ownership, or business type must be notified by filing an updated Business Registration Application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or any elective pass-through classification for corporations; a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation under the Commercial Act and Corporate Tax Act and is taxable at entity level on worldwide income. No hybrid mismatch election mechanism is available; Korean anti-avoidance rules apply by statute rather than by taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based registration threshold. Any person carrying on a taxable business in Korea must obtain VAT/business registration from business commencement irrespective of annual turnover. A simplified taxpayer status exists for small individual traders below the statutory turnover threshold, but it is not a registration exemption and is not applicable to a corporate Chusik Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: General VAT taxpayers are required to issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax system or an NTS-approved electronic tax invoice service provider. The electronic tax invoice data is filed with the NTS electronically and is available to the NTS for automated cross-matching; no physical fiscal stamp or pre-invoice government clearance applies under the Korean VAT system. Export transactions are cleared separately through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS, and NTS cross-matches the e-tax invoice and the UNI-PASS export declaration. Failure to issue or transmit an electronic tax invoice attracts additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from the Korean customs territory qualify for VAT zero-rating when (a) the supply is made by a VAT-registered Korean seller whose registration number appears on the export declaration, (b) the seller has filed an export declaration through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS in its own name, (c) the goods are actually removed from Korea to a foreign destination and the foreign buyer receives control or possession, and (d) the sales contract, commercial invoice, payment terms, bill of lading quantities, grade (Copper Cathode Grade A), and foreign exchange repatriation records are internally consistent. A mere domestic transfer or change of ownership of an LME warehouse warrant without a Korean customs export does not qualify. Cross-border services are zero-rated only when the place of supply is outside Korea or the services are used wholly outside Korea by a foreign business or user; offshore digital services effectively used by Korean consumers remain subject to Korean VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, including the export clearance certificate and export customs number

Ocean Bill of Lading (original or electronic equivalent) issued by the carrier showing the Korean VAT-registered exporter as shipper and the foreign buyer as consignee, with port-to-port details from a Korean port to a non-Korean destination
Commercial invoice, packing list, contract or Letter of Credit, and LME warrant transfer documents for Grade A copper cathodes, matching the declared customs value, weight, marks, and lot numbers

Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency in the exporter's Korean bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and KCS cross-verify each zero-rated export by matching the UNI-PASS export declaration, bill of lading date, e-tax invoice, sale contract, and the foreign exchange settlement record. If the exporter cannot produce the complete documentation package or the foreign currency proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory period, the zero rate is overturned, the supply is reclassified as domestic taxable, output VAT at 10% is assessed, related input VAT credits are denied, and additional tax plus interest is collected under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes. Where false invoices or forged export documents are used, the matter is referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment or fines, and the tax assessment period is extended up to 10 years for deceitful or unlawful acts, creating a retrospective clawback exposure on all claimed zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) reporting system
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a dual-account system in which the Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, such as trade in goods, trade settlements, and service payments, but remains subject to authorization and reporting requirements for capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, cross-border loans, and portfolio flows. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires all cross-border payments to be routed through authorized foreign exchange banks, and Korea's foreign exchange concentration system had been largely dismantled since the 1990s, but mandatory surrender requirements for export proceeds were eliminated; exporters are permitted to hold foreign currency in designated foreign currency accounts, provided that the underlying export transaction is reported to the designated bank. However, profit remittances by a foreign-invested company, such as dividends to non-resident shareholders, require proof of foreign direct investment (FDI) registration with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) and a Foreign Exchange Bank, and dividend remittances need to follow the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The Bank of Korea may impose temporary measures restricting capital flows in the event of currency crisis or excessive volatility, and the Korean government can implement 'macroprudential stability charges' on non-deposit foreign currency liabilities, so a copper cathode trading entity must carefully document all underlying physical trade contracts, LME warehouse receipts, and customs declarations to ensure convertibility and remittance on the current account remains unimpeded. In practice, for a wholesale physical commodity trader, routine trade payments and receipts are considered current account operations and are freely convertible, but any equity injection, shareholder loan, or hedging contract exceeding certain thresholds requires prior reporting to the relevant foreign exchange bank and, if the amount exceeds USD 50 million, may require BOK approval. Corporate treasury planning should therefore separate operational trade flows from capital account transactions, with each route maintaining distinct evidence files and reporting codes under the FEIN system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory statutory surrender ratio or statutory time limit requiring conversion of export proceeds into Korean won under the current Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; exporters must receive and settle export proceeds through an authorized foreign exchange bank within 5 business days after the scheduled payment due date under the underlying trade contract, or if no due date is specified, within 5 business days from the date of shipment. The exporter is allowed to retain the foreign currency in a domestic foreign currency account without forced conversion, but each receipt must be reported using the standard trade settlement reporting code (e.g., trade payment notification under FEIN) within the bank's reporting window, and any non-export related credit to a foreign currency account is strictly prohibited.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. South Korean banking law does not recognize digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) charters from foreign jurisdictions as authorized foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Fintech EMIs that hold e-money licenses in the EEA or UK are legally barred from servicing a Korean-resident corporate entity for inbound KRW settlement, trade documentation, capital verification, or FX conversion purposes because the Bank of Korea and the Financial Supervisory Service require all cross-border payments to be cleared through licensed banks in Korea. A foreign EMI may provide ancillary services such as multi-currency virtual accounts or payment aggregation, but these cannot replace the bank account required for the entity's registered capital escrow, customs-duty payments, or VAT refund processing. The only remote-digital route is through a domestic Korean internet-only bank offering corporate accounts, such as K bank or Toss Bank, provided the entity has a Korean tax ID and statutory director identity verification, but legacy tier-1 banks remain the sole viable counterparties for documentary LC transactions involving LME copper cathode warrants.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A statutory director (registered in Korea) must physically appear at the designated tier-1 branch for the initial bank onboarding to execute the corporate signatures, provide passport or national ID, corporate registration certificate, and the company seal impression. Remote opening by consular proxy is generally not recognized by Korean banks for a Chusik Hoesa; the bank's compliance team requires face-to-face confirmation under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and the anti-money laundering guidelines of the Financial Action Task Force. For a non-resident director or shareholder, the bank may allow the initial interview to be conducted at a Korean overseas branch (e.g., KB Kookmin Bank's New York or London branch) if the bank has a global branch network, but the final account activation is contingent on the submission of a power of attorney notarized at a Korean consulate and the physical visit of a local finance manager or representative to the domestic branch within the stipulated onboarding period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The entity is a newly formed Chusik Hoesa with no Korean operating history, and the sole business scope is high-value wholesale copper cathode trading, which triggers enhanced due diligence under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act because commodity trade is frequently used for trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full corporate formation package including the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, the register of directors and shareholders with full beneficial ownership declarations up to the ultimate natural person, audited opening balance sheet or bank certificate of paid-in capital, a notarized business plan with the underlying physical copper supply and offtake contracts, evidence of commercial substance such as a leased office in Korea or a registered local trading desk, and a detailed transaction flowchart for future LME warrant deliveries accompanied by the original supplier's invoice, bill of lading, customs entry, and certificate of origin for each shipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The final beneficial owner is a foreign national or foreign corporate entity located in a jurisdiction where the beneficial ownership structure may be considered opaque by the Korean bank's AML committee, particularly if the shareholder is a shell company in a tax-haven
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the consolidated organizational chart showing each intermediate entity in the ownership chain, the certificate of good standing from each registry, tax identification numbers for every entity, notarized copies of the passports or national ID cards of all directors and shareholders, and compliance with FATCA/CRS declarations if applicable, along with a written explanatory memorandum proving the ultimate beneficial owner's source of funds used for the paid-in capital injection, supported by audited financial statements of the parent company or proven liquidation proceeds from a legitimate asset sale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank's automated red-flag engine may flag Korea's nonferrous metal wholesale industry as a 'potential trade-based money laundering sector' because copper cathodes are high-value, low-mass goods, and the trading pattern involves LME warehouse receipts that can be rapidly transferred without physical movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete trade verification package comprising the commercial invoice, proforma invoice, LME warrant transfer confirmation from the recognized London Metal Exchange warehouse, Non-Ferrous Metals Association shipment inspection certificates, and a third-party commodity inspection report (e.g., SGS or Alfred H Knight) confirming the copper cathode grade and purity, alongside a written standard operating procedure for the entity's trade execution indicating that every delivery will be matched against a physical purchase contract and customs clearance record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The proposed gross sales volume of copper cathodes may exceed the disclosed paid-in capital by a multiple, triggering the bank Wealth Management and Corporate Banking Department's capital adequacy assessment for potential overdraft or trade-finance facility misuse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a cash flow forecast model showing a clear purchase-payment-to-sale-receipt cycle, a master supply agreement with a reputable smelter such as LG Chem or a Chilean producer, a master offtake agreement, and evidence of pre-negotiated letter of credit limits with a global counterpart, plus a Board resolution authorizing the opening of trade finance facilities and an undertaking that all transactions will follow the stated payment rails.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound capital injection for the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be routed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The entity first files a 'Foreign Investment Report' through the integrated system of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or the designated foreign exchange bank; the bank then issues a certificate of foreign investment after receipt of the inward remittance into a capital escrow account, which must be denominated in KRW. The wire instruction must include the investor's name, the foreign investment purpose code (e.g., '100' for acquisition of shares), and the original statement that the funds are a foreign direct investment. The inward remittance will be credited to the escrow account and the bank will verify the amount against the reported investment declaration before transferring the funds to the company's basic operating account. The bank must record the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) within 3 business days. For any inbound injection exceeding KRW 1 billion (approximately USD 750,000), the company should also prepare the Standard Foreign Investment Notification Form, a notarized investment agreement, and a board resolution of the Korean company.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound trade disbursements include the following: (1) SWIFT MT103 for low-value, high-frequency supplier payments under the purchase order, where the Korean company instructs its foreign exchange bank to debit its KRW account and credit the beneficiary in USD, subject to FEIN reporting and supply of the underlying commercial invoice and contract reference; (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) for copper cathode purchases against LME warrant delivery, typically an irrevocable, transferable or back-to-back L/C opened by the Korean company's bank in favor of the foreign smelter, with presentation documents including the original bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, weight certificate, and the LME warrant; and (3) Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) used for repeat counterparties with an established credit history, where the Korean bank sends the documents through the remitting bank and upon acceptance the payment is executed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Trade settlement in KRW is permitted for export contracts but USD/EUR settlement remains the preferred rail for international metal markets; all outbound disbursements above USD 10,000 must be supported by the relevant trade documentation, and the Korean bank will apply the 'Customs Clearance Record' verification to confirm the shipment's physical existence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Domestic KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts backed by an underlying physical copper trade exposure, with a maturity up to 12 months, requiring the bank to verify the forecasted trade flows and the hedging ratio aligning with the actual purchase and sale contracts

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may only be engaged by the Korean entity through an offshore foreign bank if the Korean parent is not a resident financial institution, but the use of NDFs is heavily restricted for onshore KRW settlement; the Bank of Korea requires all onshore KRW forwards to be settled via deliverable exchange of KRW funds, so offshore NDF hedging is not recommended without prior BOK approval

Currency swaps structured as covered interest parity transactions with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank to manage the liquidity mismatch between the USD-denominated export receivable and KRW-denominated operating costs, provided the swap is expressly tied to the physical copper trade documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convening of ordinary general meeting of shareholders for approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' general meeting (internal corporate governance act); minutes and resolutions maintained at the registered office and available to the court and National Tax Service on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each fiscal-year end; for a 31 December fiscal year, by 31 March in the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene by the deadline exposes each responsible director to administrative negligence fines up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,700); persistent failure may support judicial special liquidation or court-ordered strike-off of a dormant company under Commercial Act Article 520bis.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and tax settlement filing (including local income tax surcharge)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax system; local income tax surcharge remitted via the Ministry of the Interior and Safety local tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal-year end; for a 31 December fiscal year, by 31 March, or by 30 April where an approved extension is obtained through a licensed tax preparer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of unpaid corporate tax (30% for fraudulent non-filing); understatement penalties of 10%-40% of omitted tax; overdue surcharge at 0.022% per day on unpaid amounts; continued delinquency can lead to tax seizure, compulsory closure of the business place, revocation of tax-identification status and, after five years of no registered business, judicial strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report filing (only where audit thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission / Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the National Tax Service; audited statements also presented to shareholders at the ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The auditor must deliver the audit report to the company and file it with FSS within 14 days of delivery; audited financial statements must be presented for shareholder approval at the AGM by 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company that is legally subject to external audit and fails to appoint an auditor or file the audit report may be subject to FSS enforcement, administrative fines up to KRW 30,000,000 (approx. USD 22,200), criminal liability for responsible officers, and the annual corporate tax return may be treated as materially incomplete, triggering tax penalties and audit disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registration of annual corporate changes (e.g., changes in directors, registered office, and statutory representatives) and updating of the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local District Court Registration Office (Supreme Court corporate registration system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks from the occurrence of the relevant change (e.g., appointment or resignation of a director, change of registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration is subject to administrative negligence fines up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,700) per event; unregistered changes cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties, and repeated failure may be used by the registry court to presume dormancy for strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, independent CPA audit is mandatory for: (i) listed companies and companies whose securities are traded on a KRX exchange; (ii) unlisted companies with total assets of at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 8,900,000) at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year; (iii) unlisted companies with total assets of at least KRW 7,000,000,000 (approx. USD 5,200,000) and a debt-to-equity ratio of 500% or more; (iv) financial/credit-related companies and other entities designated by the Financial Services Commission regardless of asset size; (v) public-interest companies specifically designated by the FSC to require audit; and (vi) subsidiaries that are significant to the consolidated audit of an audited parent. Headcount alone is not a statutory audit trigger under Korean law, and there is no turnover-based audit threshold in the External Audit Act. For this copper-cathode wholesale trading entity, a mandatory audit will be triggered if the balance sheet exceeds the KRW 12,000,000,000 asset threshold or, in the case of high leverage, the KRW 7,000,000,000 asset threshold with a debt-to-equity ratio above 500%. In addition, banks and LME/LC counterparties may contractually require audited financial statements for credit facilities or documentary letter-of-credit lines even where the statutory threshold is not reached.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Mandatory audited companies must prepare statutory financial statements in accordance with Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) where required, or the accounting standards adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board for unlisted entities (K-GAAP), as applicable. Financial statements for the National Tax Service and the registry must be expressed in Korean Won and in the Korean language; English-translated statements may be prepared for LME warrant transfers, overseas banks, and cross-border counterparties as a valuation support file, but the statutory filing remains the Korean-language K-IFRS/K-GAAP financial statement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Commercial Act, there is no separate annual beneficial-ownership return filed with the company registry; however, the Chusik Hoesa must maintain an accurate register of members at its registered office, and bearer shares are prohibited. Each transfer of shares must be entered in the register of members without delay; non-registration with the company prevents the transferee from exercising rights against the company. Any resulting change in officers or other registered matters must be filed with the local District Court Registration Office within two weeks. For foreign shareholders, acquisitions or transfers of shares meeting the statutory foreign-investment threshold (generally 10% or more of voting shares or an investment of KRW 100 million or more, subject to exemptions) must be reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA, with a post-transaction report due within 30 days of the triggering event. Financial institutions also undertake periodic real-name beneficial-owner verification for corporate bank accounts under Korean AML law, and the company must cooperate with those requests; no quasi-annual UBO filing fee applies.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax top marginal rate; 26.4% aggregate after 10% local income tax surcharge
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive national rate at 9% for first KRW 200 million of taxable income; foreign investment incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; free economic zone tax reductions; R&D and job-creation tax credits; technology-transfer income 50% deduction; temporary investment tax credits; no mandatory minimum capital means a low-capital brass-plate entity can still be at full CIT risk

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Main Form 1 Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Schedule) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal; foreign non-resident filers also attach an international transaction disclosure and financial statements in Korean accounting standards.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations with prior-year corporate tax payable exceeding KRW 5 million also file semi-annual estimated tax prepayments in August and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year close; a calendar-year copper cathode wholesaler must file no later than 31 March of the following tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification and total taxable income declaration header
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the HomeTax business registration number and the Korean agent or tax representative of the foreign legal entity; failure to name a domestic tax representative can block the DTA relief and create a default withholding obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year end and accounting basis (accrual or cash)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean GAAP and the Corporate Tax Act require accrual accounting; for LME copper cathode trades, record revenue when documents are accepted under the documentary LC, not when the sea waybill or LME warrant is transferred if significant risks remain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales and revenue, net of returns and allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the full invoiced copper cathode sale price in KRW, translating USD-denominated LME warrant sales at the accrual-date exchange rate; do not net out hedging gains or documentary LC fees unless properly classified.

Cost of copper cathodes includes the LME warrant purchase price, broker and exchange fees, freight, insurance, warehouse charges and import duties; related-party purchase amounts above arm's length must be adjusted to fair value and supported by a transfer pricing file before claiming the cost deduction.

A cross-border arbitrage trader should earn a functional markup equal to the return of a routine trader under TNMM; a zero-risk booking entity with no CIGA will have its gross profit recharacterized as commission income and challenged.

Include only expenses substantiated by invoices and bank records; management fees paid to the head office or foreign related party must be disallowed unless they satisfy the profit-contribution, arm's length, and documentation requirements under Korean TP rules.

Reconcile operating income to the audited income statement; for non-resident taxpayers, no branch-level operating expense deduction can be claimed without transfer pricing documentation and a Korean VAT/LC trail.

Foreign exchange gains or losses from USD-denominated LME settlements, interest income, impairment of receivables and penalties are declared here; exchange gains are taxable and cannot be offset against unreported capital leakage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before prior-year loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If intercompany copper cathode sales exceed the statutory related-party threshold, attach the Integrated International Transaction Report and prove that the margin is not captive profit; otherwise the NTS will adjust taxable income upward.

Deduct eligible net operating losses brought forward within the 5-year limit; losses of a foreign head office cannot be set off against a Korean permanent establishment unless actually attributable to the Korean business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable bracket and national corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the graduated rates to remaining taxable income: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% above KRW 200 million, 21% above KRW 20 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion; include a local income tax surcharge schedule.

Non-residents may claim foreign tax credits and R&D credits only with the statutory documentary proof; prepayments already made under the semi-annual estimation system are credited here, and insufficient prepayment triggers interest.

Finally compute net corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge; include surcharges for late filing or under-reporting and clearly segregate the amount subject to WHT when profits are later remitted to the foreign shareholder.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% non-filing surcharge on the final corporate tax payable; negligent understatement attracts an additional 10% surcharge; fraudulent concealment attracts a 40% surcharge; late payment attracts daily 0.025% delinquency penalty from the statutory due date to settlement. If the added tax understatement exceeds the criminal threshold, the NTS refers the case under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, exposing the company and directors to imprisonment and fines; chronic delinquents are also subjected to public blacklisting and travel bans.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate non-resident withholding (20% corporate income tax withholding plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national WHT, equal to an additional 2 percentage points).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on outbound dividends, interest or royalties, the non-resident payee must (i) submit to the Korean payer a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the resident country, (ii) file or present the Non-Resident Income Tax Exemption/Reduction Application through the payer's withholding portal before the remittance date, (iii) prove beneficial ownership and absence of intermediary back-to-back arrangements, and (iv) provide substance evidence that the recipient has the capacity, staff, and economic function to hold the investment. Retroactive relief may be obtained by filing a tax refund claim within the statutory claim period if the lower treaty rate was not applied at settlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are 20% for interest and 20% for royalties, plus 2% local income tax surcharge, making the aggregate 22%. Under most Korea DTA networks, treaty rates may reduce interest to 0% to 15%, royalties to 10% to 15%, and dividends to 5% to 10% if the recipient holds at least 10% to 25% of the Korean payer's share capital and satisfies the LOB / beneficial ownership tests.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 annual aggregate of specified international related-party transactions for Local File preparation and the Integrated International Transaction Report; Master File documentation is mandatory when the worldwide consolidated group's international transactions exceed KRW 100,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not adopt an UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation, but the substance-over-form, actual business management, Limitation on Benefits and Central Management and Control doctrines are applied by the National Tax Service. A Chusik Hoesa engaged in LME copper cathode wholesale arbitrage must carry on Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea, including negotiating master purchase/sale contracts, conducting physical inventory and warehouse controls, managing price and FX risk, issuing LME warrants, taking commodity risk, and settling documentary LCs. A brass-plate invoice middleman lacks CIGA and will lose treaty benefits, be treated as a pass-through, and have income imputed to the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting KRW-denominated copper cathode LME arbitrage revenue, fabricating fake intercompany purchase invoices, inflating inventory costs of Grade A refined copper cathodes, or destroying documents to move profit from the 24% top bracket to the 9% SME bracket.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, Articles 9 and 10, fraudulent tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 2 years and, for aggravated evasion exceeding KRW 300 million, up to 5 years, with fines up to five times the evaded tax; the NTS additionally imposes a 40% fraudulent understatement surcharge under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who approved the false account books can be personally assessed under the National Tax Collection Act secondary taxpayer doctrine; personal assets can be seized after disregard of the corporate entity; the director faces a departure ban and blacklisting for unpaid tax exceeding KRW 50 million and can be sentenced to imprisonment, thereby piercing the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse and Hollow Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Integrated International Transaction Report when annual related-party copper transactions exceed KRW 5 billion, submitting a Local File without functional analysis or comparables, pricing copper cathode cross-border sales below CUP, or using a Korean intermediary with no staff to book an arbitrage margin controlled by the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Tax Adjustment Act, failure to report or submitting false intercompany transaction disclosures triggers a 10% surcharge on the undisclosed transaction value, increased to 20% for false information; transfer pricing adjustments carry statutory overdue interest and can be treated as undisclosed foreign income, with additional surcharges up to 40% of the tax understatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who prepared fraudulent TP files can be held jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax, interest and penalties; the tax court can recharacterize the arrangement and pierce the company if the Korean entity lacks CIGA; directors also risk criminal charges for obstruction of tax administration, travel blacklisting, and civil restitution of diverted profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trade-Based Money Laundering and AML Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using over-invoicing, under-invoicing or fictitious LME warrant transfers through the Chusik Hoesa's settlement account to wash funds, relying on back-to-back documentary LCs without economic trade, or failing to report suspicious transactions arising from copper cathode arbitrage to Korea's financial intelligence unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, failure to report suspicious transactions is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 30 million, with confiscation of proceeds; aggravated trade-based money laundering involving more than KRW 1 billion can exceed the statutory fine range and trigger freezing orders and liquidation remedies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and AML compliance director are individually prosecutable; civil asset restitution is available to defrauded LC counterparties; courts may pierce the corporate veil when the Chusik Hoesa is operated as a mere façade, and a travel ban can be imposed during the criminal investigation.
